newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy pensions bill above EU average -Istat.
newsitem.headline: Italy pensions bill above EU average -Istat.

text.p: Italy spends more than any other European Union country on pension benefits and the bill is set to climb unless reforms are introduced, Italy's statistical institute Istat said in its annual report released on Wednesday.

While Italy's total welfare spending is lower than the European Union average, spending on old age pensions stood at 13 percent of gross domestic product in 1994, almost three percent more than the EU average, Istat said.

"Reforms from recent years are bringing about a containment of spending, but there are still some worrying elements for the future, both for the sustainability of expenditure and the fairness of the system" Istat said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi opened talks with union leaders on Tuesday at the start of what are expected to be lengthy negotiations over fresh welfare and pension reform.

As life expectancy continues to grow, "there could be a strong increase in the burden of pension and health spending," Istat warned. It said the average length pensions were drawn would grow by as much as 10 percent between now and 2020.
By contrast, spending on health slipped to 7.5 percent of GDP from 8.1 percent in 1991 and very few benefits were aimed at the unemployed or families, Istat said.
"Social benefits tend to favour older people at the expense of the young," the Istat report said.
Total welfare spending represented 24.2 percent of GDP in 1994 against a European average of 27.4 percent. -- Rome newsroom +396 6792501
